source.title: When Does Muon Actually Win? A Paired Data-, Time-, and Tuning-Budget Benchmark
source.authors: Mushir Akhtar; H. Nounou; M. Mansouri; M. Nounou

record.tranche_reason: Extends optimizer comparisons to Muon versus AdamW on small language and vision models, reporting validation and test performance under data and time budgets.
record.gate_note: The paper compares optimizers and reports validation and test outcomes, so it bears on the claim's optimizer condition. It does not test random-label memorization, width beyond interpolation, convolutional versus fully connected networks, large-batch effects, dropout, magnitude-aware sharpness, or removal of memorized examples. The specific SGD-versus-adaptive comparison in V4 is not tested.
record.test_reason: The study compares Muon with AdamW, not adaptive optimizers with SGD or momentum SGD as V4 specifies. Its switching and variance-adaptation experiments also do not supply that comparison. No other version is tested. Held-out loss is a relevant measure for V4; the missing comparator, rather than the absence of a training-to-test gap, prevents linking these results to it.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: Muon improves data-budget performance on all four tested workloads, while equal-time validation AUC favors Muon on vision and AdamW on language. These rankings concern selected configurations, small models, and reference kernels on one A100; the listed implementation and architecture factors are scope conditions, not independently established causes.
record.recipe_differences: Compares Muon with AdamW using paired matched initializations, equal-data and equal-time trajectories, and test-loss evaluation; it does not use the SGD-versus-adaptive optimizer comparisons specified in V4.
record.method_sensitivity: The equal-time optimizer ranking differs between language and vision workloads; tuning-regret estimates depend on candidate pools, their construction, development seed, and uniform sampling rule.

fits_no_version.finding: Muon reduces equal-data validation-loss AUC by 3.25–22.44% and final test loss by 4.77–26.03%. Equal-time validation AUC favors AdamW on both language workloads and Muon on both vision workloads.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Muon versus AdamW performance rankings depend on the workload and whether the budget holds processed data or training time fixed.

fits_no_version.finding: On language-micro, the full Muon optimizer call consumes 63.07% of training time versus 8.84% for AdamW.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Reference optimizer implementations can differ substantially in their share of training runtime.

record.peer_reviewed: OPT2026: 18th Annual Workshop on Optimization for Machine Learning
record.problems: Five paired seeds in the primary study; selection uses one seed; short training horizons; fixed candidate pools; one accelerator and reference kernels. Training error is not reported, so the training-to-test gap cannot be assessed. The authors caution against extrapolating wall-clock results to larger models or optimized implementations.
record.rows_left_out: Optimizer timing and throughput entries for the other three workloads, equal-time endpoint-loss rows, and secondary-strategy and tuning-budget results are not extracted; the primary comparisons already show workload-dependent optimizer outcomes, and the main measure requested by the claim is not the training-to-test gap.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting, natural-label generalization, and chance-level held-out performance with random labels.
Widening beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive methods versus SGD or momentum SGD under limited or broader tuning; recovery through decoupled weight decay or switching to SGD; word-level language-model comparisons.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that remove their penalty.
Dropout interventions and their dependence on training-set size, augmentation, and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, generalization gaps, and comparisons with norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus removing equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: Change the record's tests/T3 classification to discusses/T6. The secondary AdamW-to-Muon switch is not a switch to SGD. Fixed-pool tuning regret and variance-adapted Muon results do not establish V4's SGD comparison. No omitted result in the supplied text requires a claim-linked missing entry.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Width sweep beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD or momentum SGD; broader tuning, weight-decay variants, switching, and word-level language comparisons.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and recipe changes.
Dropout effects and interaction with data augmentation or weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and comparison with norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the resulting test accuracy.
